drivers.why: Driver. The long-dated inventory pool is the only Part One finding that both skeptics left standing as a move: it ties up cash Merck is now borrowing to replace, it kept growing after the tariff delay that was its stated reason, and a product split plus a capped, net-of-reserve release is a step the CFO controls without a counterparty.

net.text: Net over 24 months: expected interest of $18.7M less the $7.5M cost is $11.2M pre-tax, plus an expected one-time cash release of $0.43B, which is zero if the review finds no sellable surplus. Part 1's Sharpest Needle, the IRS transition-tax NOPAs of about $1.56B before interest ($1.3B of tax plus $260M of penalties), does not drive this move: both skeptics killed the tax move because Merck is already contesting the NOPAs, resolution may take a number of years, and a reserved penalty would come back as a non-cash reserve release. The cash plan keeps that exposure separate: even the full $1.0B release would cover only 64% of the $1.56B, Merck already carries $546M of accrued interest and penalties, and any tax payment would come from the $8,363M of cash and investments at June 30, 2026, not from the release, which retires debt. Interest on any tax owed is left unsized: the IRS rate page is not yet in the index.

rejected.move: Fund a U.S. field program converting Keytruda IV patients to Keytruda Qlex, or its narrowed pilot in IV-chemotherapy combination regimens.

why_passed.text: Management already says it is on track to reach 30% to 40% peak adoption of Keytruda Qlex by end of 2027 and has a contracting strategy to make conversion frictionless, so a funded program adds nothing the company has not announced and paid for. The label's crossover data cover monotherapy only, the draft doctor piece left out the route-specific administration-reaction warning, and the CFO lens found the narrowed chemotherapy-combination pilot earns no return inside 24 months.

unresolved.topic: What the long-dated inventory pool holds, and whether a release arrives as cash or as reserve charges
unresolved.cfo_position: No page ties the pool to tariff staging or to reshoring bridge stock; the reshoring reading is an inference too. The release math holds for any slice proven sellable at cost, so diagnose first and size the release on the sellable surplus only.
unresolved.decider_position: Management is choosing to build: the pool grew after the tariff delay, which the filing ties to reshoring, and reserves are rising. Investors cannot verify any target until Merck discloses the split in the inventory note, so disclosure must come before any target, and the release must be counted net of reserve charges.

unresolved.topic: Severity of the Qlex re-pricing candidate
unresolved.cfo_position: Fatal on its own numbers: certain forgone revenue inside the window against a smaller benefit after it, negative through the end of the decade whoever decides. The CFO round-two summary still describes the decider as rating it major.
unresolved.decider_position: Rated it major in round one for the wrong-decider and wrong-lever reasons, then conceded fatal in round two once the CFO's net-negative math was in; the two files agree on fatal but give different reasons (math versus decider and lever).

unresolved.topic: Whether CMS Part B payment-limit rows may size a decision when cited only by locator
unresolved.cfo_position: Machine-data rows cannot be quoted but can be cited by locator and are fit for sizing; the cross-quarter Qlex premium check used them that way.
unresolved.decider_position: Did not open the rows beyond their locators and treats the cross-quarter premium only as a reason the re-price is sized to one quarter, not as a quoted fact to size a move on.

unresolved.topic: Target segment for any salvage pilot of the Qlex conversion candidate
unresolved.cfo_position: Round one: monotherapy and oral-combination practices, where early use clusters. Round two: no segment earns a return inside the window, so any pilot is a post-patent-expiry option, not a funded return.
unresolved.decider_position: IV-chemotherapy combination regimens, the segment management says lags; a pilot in monotherapy practices, where management already converts, cannot show causation.
